title: Future of Crew Dragon weighs on commercial spaceflight industry
summary: SpaceX acknowledges the remaining lifespan of its Crew Dragon fleet but remains uncertain about its future operations. The uncertainty impacts the broader commercial spaceflight industry.

title: SpaceX’s new Starfall program offers validation and competition for reentry startups
summary: SpaceX launched its new Starfall program with a test flight of a commercial reentry capsule on June 23, aiming to validate and compete in the growing microgravity research and manufacturing market. The initiative positions SpaceX as a key player in the emerging reentry startup sector.

title: Rocketdyne reemerges as standalone space company
summary: Rocketdyne has reemerged as an independent space company after AE Industrial, a private-equity firm, acquired a 60% stake while L3Harris retained a noncontrolling interest.

title: Kreios Space to fly VLEO demonstration in NanoAvionics bus
summary: Kreios Space plans to conduct the first very low Earth orbit (VLEO) demonstration of its air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) using a NanoAvionics bus. The demonstration will be supported by Kongsberg.

title: NASA, SpaceX studying how to prevent future upper stage lunar collisions
summary: NASA and SpaceX are collaborating to prevent future collisions of upper stages with the moon after a Falcon 9 upper stage is expected to impact the lunar surface this week. The study aims to address the growing concern of space debris and its potential impact on lunar missions.

title: Hughes files for bankruptcy after GEO business loses ground to Starlink
summary: Hughes, a subsidiary of EchoStar, filed for bankruptcy due to declining geostationary satellite broadband business, heavily impacted by competition from SpaceX's Starlink constellation.

title: Xona secures spectrum approval for satellite navigation network
summary: Xona has secured spectrum approval for its satellite navigation network, enabling stronger signals near GPS frequencies. This approval marks a significant step for the startup in developing its navigation services.

title: Airbus and Thales win order for SpainSat replacement
summary: Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space have secured a contract to build a replacement military communications satellite for Spain. The deal is part of ongoing efforts to establish a space joint venture involving Airbus, Thales, and Leonardo.
company: Airbus Defence and Space, Thales Alenia Space

title: U.S. Air Force expands Blue Origin rocket cargo contract
summary: The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory increased Blue Origin's contract by $11.7 million to study the use of space rockets for point-to-point deliveries. This expansion highlights growing interest in leveraging commercial space capabilities for rapid logistics.

title: Space Force awards K2 Space $22.9 million for laser communications demonstration
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded K2 Space a $22.9 million contract to demonstrate laser communications using two satellites equipped with optical terminals for military systems connectivity.

title: 'Significant areas of Mars may have once been covered by water': Scientists find hidden clue in Spirit rover data
summary: A new analysis of NASA's Spirit rover data reveals traces of crystalline hematite and altered magnetite, suggesting significant areas of Mars were once covered by water. This finding supports the theory that liquid water played a major role in shaping the Red Planet.

title: Are aliens running out of places to hide? It turns out we've searched much more of the galaxy than we realized
summary: Astronomers have discovered they may have scanned millions more stars for extraterrestrial signals than previously believed, potentially expanding the search for alien life. This revelation could lead to new methods for detecting intelligent civilizations.

title: I bought a $50 telescope on Facebook Marketplace — here's what I learned
summary: A person shares their experience of purchasing a $50 telescope from Facebook Marketplace. They reflect on what they learned from the experience.

title: This Sky-Watcher is an ideal beginner telescope for solar observing
summary: The Sky-Watcher Heliostar 76mm H-alpha is a beginner-friendly solar telescope designed for observing the sun's surface. It is praised for its portability and ease of use.

title: CNN dives into how Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos are backing NASA's race to the moon against China (exclusive clip)
summary: Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos are financially supporting NASA's efforts to return to the moon, competing against China's space ambitions. The new CNN special 'Eclipsing Power' explores how billionaires influence the global space race.

title: A SpaceX rocket will crash into the moon this week. Why is it on a collision course?
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket's upper stage is set to crash into the moon on Wednesday (Aug. 5) after being placed on a collision course. The incident raises questions about space debris management and the rocket's trajectory.

title: Jack in for a cyberpunk jolt with this energized first trailer for Apple TV's 'Neuromancer'
summary: Apple TV released the first trailer for 'Neuromancer', a cyberpunk adaptation of William Gibson's 1984 novel. This marks a significant step in bringing the influential sci-fi classic to the screen.

title: Jupiter's moon Europa may have signs of life in its buried ocean — but can we get to them?
summary: Jupiter's moon Europa may harbor signs of life in its subsurface ocean, raising questions about accessibility for future missions. Scientists emphasize the need to interpret findings and identify habitable zones for exploration.

title: 3 moons of Neptune may be remnants of ice worlds shattered in a catastrophic crash
summary: Three moons of Neptune may be remnants of ice worlds destroyed in a catastrophic collision. The discovery highlights the need for further exploration beyond Voyager 2's 1989 flyby.

title: The 1st 'three-headed' asteroid | Space photo of the day for Aug. 3, 2026
summary: Astronomers have discovered what is believed to be the first-known 'trilobate' or three-headed asteroid in our solar system, as revealed by new images. This unique celestial object presents a rare structure in asteroid formation.

title: APOD: August 4, 2026 – Curious Cometary Knots in the Helix Nebula
summary: APOD features an image of cometary knots in the Helix Nebula, showcasing a fascinating astronomical phenomenon. The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) is a daily showcase of cosmic imagery with explanations by professional astronomers.

title: Smoke Streams Across Eastern Washington
summary: Wildfires in eastern Washington in August 2026 caused severe air pollution, destroyed hundreds of structures, and led to mandatory evacuations in Spokane.

title: Louisiana Students Loft Payloads from NASA Balloon Facility in Texas
summary: Louisiana students annually launch payloads from NASA's Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility in Texas to conduct experiments at the edge of space. The initiative provides hands-on experience in engineering and data collection.

title: A Bare Summer for Barnes Ice Cap
summary: The Barnes Ice Cap on Canada's Baffin Island experienced rapid and early snow loss in summer 2026, exposing a network of melt features. This highlights ongoing glacial retreat due to climate change.

title: NASA Delivers Navigation System for Commercial Lunar Relay
summary: NASA delivered the NavCube3-mini payload to Intuitive Machines for integration into its first lunar relay satellite, Altus-1, advancing future lunar communications and navigation services. The compact navigation system will support astronauts and rovers at NASA's planned Moon Base.

title: Ike Theriot Helps Prepare Astronauts to Work on the Moon
summary: Ike Theriot leads NASA's Flight Operations Surface Testing for astronaut lunar exploration. His career path from the U.S. Army to NASA highlights discipline and determination.

title: NASA Brings Space Exploration to the FIFA World Cup
summary: NASA showcased space exploration at the FIFA World Cup's FIFA Fan Festival in Houston, attracting over 500,000 visitors and highlighting missions like Artemis and the International Space Station. The exhibit aimed to educate a global audience on how NASA's work benefits life on Earth.

title: APOD: 2026 August 3 – Vaporizing Meteor Photobombs the Lacerta Nebula
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 3, 2026, features a meteor vaporizing as it passes through the Lacerta Nebula. The image highlights a brief cosmic event captured by astronomers.

title: APOD: 2026 August 2 – A Fire Rainbow over West Virginia
summary: APOD features an image of a 'fire rainbow' over West Virginia, explained by professional astronomers. The phenomenon involves ice crystals in cirrus clouds refracting sunlight.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy with multiple space launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The launch manifest is filled with various missions from different organizations.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the ISS in 2026, pending redesign work. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted ongoing efforts to address previous issues.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase. Meanwhile, retrofitting work continues on Pad 1 for Block 3 flights.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing the rebuilding of Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket following a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: Ship 40 successfully completed its mission and returned intact during SpaceX's Starship Flight 13, demonstrating its reliability and promoting the potential for future missions.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket launch in China and a Falcon 9 mission.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io during two recent flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis Space Center's B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn for future missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX on its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's Starship development program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 mission successfully docked with the ISS, adding three new crew members. A U.S. spacewalk completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) released a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over its 50-year history. This publication celebrates the agency's milestones and contributions to space exploration.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites working in tandem to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) is hosting its Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands, where startup companies will showcase innovative space technologies and collaborate with industry leaders. The event aims to foster idea exchange, capability showcases, and partnership opportunities within Europe's space sector.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance communication and radar systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) is hosting events to discuss the implementation of decisions made at the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025 (CM25). These events aim to inform industry about planned activities, priorities, and opportunities within ESA programs.

title: Xona Clears Final Regulatory Hurdle for PNT Constellation
summary: Xona Space Systems has secured FCC approval to broadcast Pulsar navigation signals from a full satellite constellation, marking the final regulatory hurdle before scaling deployment.

title: Kreios Taps Kongsberg NanoAvionics for 2028 VLEO Demo
summary: Kreios has selected Kongsberg NanoAvionics to support its 2028 Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) demonstration mission, which aims to test the company's ABEP thruster across various altitudes below Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

title: True Anomaly Chases an Evading Target
summary: True Anomaly successfully executed the first in-space pursuit of an evading target as part of the VICTUS HAZE mission. This achievement marks a significant milestone in space operations and satellite maneuvering.

title: AFRL Adds $11.7M to Blue Origin’s Point-to-Point Cargo Contract
summary: AFRL increased Blue Origin's contract by $11.7M to study point-to-point cargo delivery missions using its launcher. The contract aims to explore the launcher's potential for rapid global logistics.

title: K2 Space Raises $500M Series D at $6.8B Valuation
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at $6.8 billion. This brings the company's total financing to over $1 billion since 2022.

title: NordSpace Funds NVD Amid Canada’s Export Push
summary: NordSpace Ventures invested in North Vector Dynamics, a company developing sovereign missile capabilities, aligning with Canada's export initiatives.

title: Report: Our Launch Cadence Forecast For Next-Gen Rockets
summary: The article discusses the expected flight cadence ramp for next-gen reusable rockets like New Glenn, Neutron, Nova, Terran R, and Eclipse. It forecasts the launch frequency of these advanced rocket systems.

title: Payload Field Guide: European Launchers
summary: Europe is rapidly developing new launch capabilities, but progress is slower than desired. The continent aims to enhance its space industry competitiveness.

title: Hop Aero Wants to Deliver Cargo via Rocket
summary: Hop Aero, a new startup, launched on Y Combinator with their autonomous suborbital rocket, Rook. The company aims to deliver cargo via rocket.

title: Payload Pioneers: Where Are They Now?
summary: The Payload Pioneers program has recognized 90 young professionals in the space industry since 2023. The article updates on the current status of some of the 30-under-30 awardees.

title: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space to Build SpainSat NG-III
summary: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space have been contracted by Hisdesat to build the SpainSat NG-III secure satellite communications satellite for Spain. Airbus, as the prime contractor, announced the award on July 31.

title: ETL Acquires Software Developer Amphinicy Technologies
summary: ETL Systems has acquired Amphinicy Technologies, a software developer specializing in satcom and Earth Observation markets. The acquisition aims to enhance ETL's ability to address complex ground segment challenges.

title: Xona Gets Approval to Deploy Commercial Navigation Constellation
summary: Xona has received FCC approval to deploy its commercial navigation constellation called Pulsar, which is planned to consist of more than 250 satellites. The company announced the authorization to broadcast radionavigation signals on Monday.

title: Hughes Files for Chapter 11 With Plan to Reorganize Around Enterprise, Defense Business
summary: Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to reorganize around enterprise, government, and defense business segments. The move aims to address a decline in consumer satellite operations.

title: AccelerCom and Eclipse Space Reveals Details of D2D Collaboration
summary: AccelerComm has completed two engineering engagements with Eclipse Space to define the physical-layer architecture for its next-generation spacecraft. This collaboration focuses on Direct-to-Device (D2D) satellite infrastructure.

title: K2 Space Secures Series D Funding After Hitting $1 Billion Contract Value Milestone
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in Series D funding, valuing the company at nearly $7 billion. This follows the company surpassing $1 billion in contract value.

title: Hispasat Obtains WTA Certification for Madrid Teleport
summary: Hispasat's Arganda del Rey Teleport in Madrid has received Tier 4 Full certification from the World Teleport Association (WTA), marking the 80th such certification issued. This achievement highlights Hispasat's commitment to high-quality teleport operations.

title: Planet Labs Wins One-Year Agricultural Data Contract with the Scottish Government
summary: Planet Labs secured a one-year, seven-figure agricultural data contract with the Scottish Government through its reseller Computacenter. The deal involves Planet's German subsidiary based in Berlin.

title: Fortastra and Hadrian Sign National Security Spacecraft Manufacturing MoU
summary: Fortastra and Hadrian signed an MoU to collaborate on building advanced spacecraft for national security missions. The partnership aims to address urgent space missions through technical collaboration.

title: Sophia Space and Caltech File Orbital Data Centers Patent
summary: Sophia Space and Caltech have been issued a patent for space-based data centers. The patent, filed in October 2024 and issued in July 2026, covers architectures for large-scale, modular orbital data centers.
